item.back: One eukaryotic cell divides to make two identical daughter cells.

evidence.quote: Mitosis is the process by which a single eukaryotic cell divides to produce two identical daughter cells.

item.back: Cytokinesis: the cytoplasm divides, giving two separate daughter cells.

evidence.quote: After mitosis, cytokinesis takes place. This is the division of the cytoplasm, producing two separate daughter cells.

item.front: How do the daughter cells compare to the parent cell?
item.back: They are genetically identical, with the same number of chromosomes.

evidence.quote: Each daughter cell is genetically identical to the parent cell, with the same number of chromosomes.

item.front: Why does the body need mitosis?
item.back: To grow, to replace old or damaged cells (like skin cells) and to heal after injury.

evidence.quote: It also replaces old or damaged cells, such as skin cells, and helps with healing after injury.
Key term: Cytokinesis - the division of the cytoplasm.
